questions.stem: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) guarantees how many days of wage employment per year to each rural household?
options: 100 days
150 days
200 days
90 days
questions.explanation: MGNREGA (enacted 2005, came into force February 2, 2006) guarantees at least 100 days of unskilled wage employment per financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work. States like Rajasthan have extended it to 150 days.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) scheme provides 35 kg of foodgrains per month at highly subsidised rates to which category?
options: All BPL families
The poorest of the poor (most destitute BPL families)
All rural families below median income
Urban slum dwellers only
questions.explanation: AAY, launched in December 2000, targets the 'poorest among the poor' — the most destitute BPL households. They receive 35 kg/month at Rs. 2/kg (wheat) and Rs. 3/kg (rice). Under NFSA 2013, AAY beneficiaries get rice/wheat/coarse grains at Rs. 3/2/1 per kg.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The Gini Coefficient is a statistical measure of:
options: GDP growth rate of an economy
Poverty headcount ratio in a country
Income or wealth inequality within a population (0 = perfect equality, 1 = perfect inequality)
Human development index ranking
questions.explanation: The Gini Coefficient (developed by Italian statistician Corrado Gini) measures income/wealth inequality. A value of 0 indicates perfect equality (everyone has equal income), while 1 indicates perfect inequality (one person has all income). It is derived from the Lorenz Curve.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: Which type of unemployment is most prevalent in India's agricultural sector, where labour productivity is near zero because more people work on farms than is actually needed?
options: Cyclical unemployment
Structural unemployment
Frictional unemployment
Disguised unemployment
questions.explanation: Disguised unemployment (also called hidden unemployment) occurs when more people are employed in a job than are actually needed. In Indian agriculture, removing a portion of the labour force would not reduce output — the 'marginal product of labour' is near zero. It is most common in subsistence farming.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The Tendulkar Committee (report 2009) revised India's poverty measurement methodology. Its key change was to:
options: Base the poverty line on Monthly Per Capita Consumption Expenditure (MPCE) covering food, health, and education — not just caloric intake
Include urban informal workers in a new BPL classification
Increase the rural caloric norm from 2,100 to 2,400 kcal/day
Replace consumption surveys with direct income surveys
questions.explanation: The Tendulkar Committee moved away from the purely calorie-based definition to a broader consumption-based poverty line that includes food, non-food essentials (health, education, clothing). This raised the poverty ratio but was considered a more realistic measure of deprivation.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The Rangarajan Committee (2014) revised the poverty line upward. The revised monthly per capita consumption expenditure (MPCE) threshold for urban areas was set at approximately:
options: Rs. 816 per month
Rs. 1,407 per month
Rs. 972 per month
Rs. 1,200 per month
questions.explanation: The Rangarajan Committee revised the poverty line upward: Rs. 972/month per capita for rural areas and Rs. 1,407/month for urban areas. This was significantly higher than the Tendulkar Committee's estimates and led to a higher poverty count (~29.5% vs Tendulkar's ~21.9%).
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best example of seasonal unemployment?
options: A factory worker laid off due to an economic recession
An IT professional searching for a new job after leaving her previous one
A sugarcane cutter with no employment during the off-harvest (non-crushing) season
A coal miner displaced by the shift to solar energy
questions.explanation: Seasonal unemployment occurs when people are unemployed at certain seasons of the year (e.g., agricultural labourers in the rabi/kharif off-seasons, sugarcane cutters during the off-crushing season, workers in tourism at non-peak times). It is a structural feature of agrarian economies.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The Human Development Index (HDI), published annually by UNDP, measures human development along which three dimensions?
options: Income, education, and gender equality
Income, health, and environmental sustainability
Education, infrastructure, and governance quality
Long and healthy life (health), knowledge (education), and decent standard of living (income)
questions.explanation: HDI is calculated using: (1) Life expectancy index (health/long life); (2) Education index (mean years of schooling + expected years); and (3) GNI per capita index (standard of living). It was developed by Mahbub ul Haq and Amartya Sen.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) was enacted in which year?
questions.explanation: MGNREGA was enacted by Parliament on August 25, 2005 and came into force on February 2, 2006. It was initially launched in 200 of the most backward districts and was extended to the entire country by April 2008. It is the world's largest employment guarantee scheme.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: Under the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013, priority households receive subsidized foodgrains at which rates?
options: Rs. 2/kg wheat, Rs. 3/kg rice, Rs. 1/kg coarse grains — paid by beneficiary
Rs. 3/kg rice, Rs. 2/kg wheat, Rs. 1/kg coarse grains — paid by beneficiary
Rs. 1/kg for all grains (rice, wheat, and coarse grains)
Market price minus a 50% subsidy
questions.explanation: Under NFSA 2013, Priority Households (PHH) receive 5 kg/person/month at: rice — Rs. 3/kg, wheat — Rs. 2/kg, coarse grains — Rs. 1/kg. AAY households get 35 kg/household at the same prices. (PM-GKAY later provided grains free of cost.)
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The Lorenz Curve is a graphical tool used to represent:
options: GDP growth trend over time
Unemployment rate variation by age group
Cumulative income distribution — showing how income is shared across population percentiles
Poverty headcount ratio by state
questions.explanation: The Lorenz Curve plots the cumulative share of income (y-axis) against the cumulative share of the population ranked by income (x-axis). The 45° diagonal represents perfect equality; the Gini Coefficient is the area between the diagonal and the Lorenz Curve, divided by the total area under the diagonal.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), launched in August 2014 with a 'financial inclusion' objective, primarily aims at:
options: Providing free housing to BPL families
Providing subsidised foodgrains to poor households
Providing 100 days of guaranteed employment to rural households
Opening bank accounts for the unbanked population and providing them financial services
questions.explanation: PMJDY is India's financial inclusion programme — it provides universal banking access by opening basic savings bank accounts (with zero balance), offering RuPay debit cards, accidental insurance, and life insurance cover. It is a prerequisite for Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT).
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: 'Frictional unemployment' refers to:
options: Temporary unemployment arising when workers are transitioning between jobs or new entrants are seeking first employment
Unemployment caused by economic recession or falling aggregate demand
Unemployment due to skill mismatch with available job vacancies
Unemployment in agriculture during the lean/off season
questions.explanation: Frictional unemployment is a short-term form arising from the normal labour market transitions — workers leaving old jobs to find better ones, new graduates searching for their first job. It is considered 'natural' unemployment and exists even in a healthy economy.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: Using the Tendulkar Committee methodology, the approximate poverty ratio in India in 2011-12 was:
questions.explanation: The Planning Commission (using Tendulkar Committee methodology) estimated India's poverty ratio at 21.9% in 2011-12 — down from 37.2% in 2004-05. This translates to about 270 million people below the poverty line.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission in January 2015. What does 'NITI' stand for?
options: National Institute of Technology and Industry
New Infrastructure and Transformation Initiative
National Institution for Transforming India
National Initiative for Technology Integration
questions.explanation: NITI stands for National Institution for Transforming India. Unlike the Planning Commission, NITI Aayog functions as a policy think tank, providing strategic direction and fostering cooperative federalism. It does not allocate plan funds to States/Ministries.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: Which Nobel Prize-winning economist is associated with the 'capability approach' to poverty, which argues that poverty is the deprivation of basic capabilities and freedoms — not merely low income?
options: John Maynard Keynes
Milton Friedman
Amartya Sen
Jeffrey Sachs
questions.explanation: Amartya Sen (Nobel Prize in Economics, 1998) developed the capability approach, arguing that poverty means the inability to lead a minimally decent life due to lack of basic capabilities (to be well-nourished, literate, participate in community life, etc.). This influenced the UNDP's HDI framework.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: 'Structural unemployment' arises primarily due to:
options: Workers voluntarily moving between jobs in a tight labour market
Seasonal fluctuations in labour demand
Cyclical downturn reducing overall employment demand
Mismatch between workers' skills and the skills required for available job vacancies
questions.explanation: Structural unemployment results from a fundamental mismatch between the qualifications or skills workers have and those demanded by employers. It is long-term and requires retraining. In India, it is exacerbated by slow educational system adaptation to industry needs.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI), co-developed by UNDP and Oxford OPHI, considers deprivations along which three broad dimensions?
options: Health, Education, and Living Standards
Income, Employment, and Housing
Gender equity, Environment, and Governance
Food security, Safe water, and Energy access
questions.explanation: The Global MPI covers 10 indicators across 3 dimensions: Health (nutrition, child mortality), Education (years of schooling, school attendance), and Living Standards (cooking fuel, sanitation, water, electricity, housing, assets). A household is 'MPI poor' if deprived in ≥33% of weighted indicators.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The Public Distribution System (PDS) in India distributes foodgrains to BPL and AAY card holders through which mechanism?
options: Direct cash transfers to beneficiary bank accounts
A network of Fair Price Shops (ration shops) across the country
Mobile food distribution vans operated by FCI
NGO-managed community distribution points
questions.explanation: The PDS operates through approximately 5 lakh Fair Price Shops (FPS/ration shops) that are licensed dealers distributing subsidised foodgrains (rice, wheat, coarse grains, sugar, kerosene) to eligible card holders. FCI supplies the grains to state governments, who distribute through FPS.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The National Sample Survey Office (NSSO) in India is the primary source of data for estimating:
options: GDP and national income accounts
Balance of payments and external trade
Household consumption expenditure and poverty estimates
Industrial production and manufacturing output
questions.explanation: NSSO (now merged into NSO — National Statistical Office) conducts large-scale household surveys on consumption expenditure, employment-unemployment, and living conditions. Its Consumer Expenditure Surveys are the basis for poverty line estimates and Gini calculations in India.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: 'Cyclical unemployment' is caused by:
options: Workers moving voluntarily between jobs
Skills mismatch in the labour market
Seasonal variations in agricultural demand
Decline in economic activity during a recession, which reduces aggregate demand for labour
questions.explanation: Cyclical unemployment (also called demand-deficient unemployment) rises during recessions when falling aggregate demand leads firms to lay off workers, and falls during economic booms. Keynesian economics recommends fiscal stimulus to reduce cyclical unemployment.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) scheme primarily aims to:
options: Provide free housing to below-poverty-line families with children
Reduce child malnutrition, improve child health, and promote early childhood development and care
Ensure 100% school enrollment for children aged 6-14
Provide skill training to adolescent girls and boys
questions.explanation: ICDS (launched 1975) is one of India's flagship programmes for early childhood development. Through Anganwadi centres, it provides supplementary nutrition, immunisation, health check-ups, referral services, pre-school education, and nutrition and health education to children under 6 and pregnant/lactating mothers.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: Under the PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PM-GKAY) and subsequent NFSA provisioning, eligible beneficiaries receive foodgrains at:
options: Zero cost (free of charge) under PM-GKAY, which was later integrated into NFSA free grain provisioning from 2024
Highly subsidised rates of Rs. 1-2/kg
50% below market price
Market price minus Central Issue Price subsidy
questions.explanation: PM-GKAY, launched in March 2020 as Covid relief, provided free food grains (5 kg/person/month, over and above NFSA entitlement). From January 2024, free foodgrains to all 81 crore NFSA beneficiaries (Priority HH + AAY) were made permanent under a unified scheme at zero cost.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The original calorie-based poverty norm in India, which set 2,400 kcal/day per person for rural areas and 2,100 kcal/day for urban areas, was established by which body?
options: Rangarajan Committee (2014)
Tendulkar Committee (2009)
Alagh Committee (1979) / Task Force on Projection of Minimum Needs
Lakdawala Committee (1993)
questions.explanation: The Lakdawala Committee (1993), using the original 1979 Task Force norms (Alagh Committee), anchored the Indian poverty line to daily caloric requirements: 2,400 kcal/day (rural) and 2,100 kcal/day (urban). The Tendulkar Committee later moved away from this single-dimensional caloric approach.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 1 — adopted by the UN — targets the elimination of:
options: Gender inequality in education
Child mortality under age 5
Extreme poverty (living on less than $2.15/day PPP) for all people everywhere by 2030
Air pollution-related deaths globally
questions.explanation: SDG 1 ('No Poverty') aims to end extreme poverty (defined as living on less than $2.15/day at 2017 purchasing power parity) for all people everywhere by 2030. It also targets reducing poverty by at least half using national definitions, and implementing social protection systems.
